objects.description: This header (chafa.h) is an umbrella header that only includes other Chafa public headers and defines no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes by itself. All custom types are defined in the included headers, not here.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaCanvasConfig ChafaCanvasConfig;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a canvas configuration object used by Chafa to control rendering parameters (geometry, color handling, dithering, pixel/canvas modes, symbol maps, etc.). The struct is forward-declared and defined elsewhere; it is reference-counted via ref/unref in this API.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaCanvas ChafaCanvas;
objects.description: Opaque canvas object representing an internal image/cell buffer used by Chafa to draw and print terminal graphics. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the structure is defined privately. Lifetime is managed by chafa_canvas_ref/unref; instances are created with chafa_canvas_new or chafa_canvas_new_similar.

objects.definition:
typedef enum
{
    /* 32 bits per pixel */

    CHAFA_PIXEL_RGBA8_PREMULTIPLIED,
    CHAFA_PIXEL_BGRA8_PREMULTIPLIED,
    CHAFA_PIXEL_ARGB8_PREMULTIPLIED,
    CHAFA_PIXEL_ABGR8_PREMULTIPLIED,

    CHAFA_PIXEL_RGBA8_UNASSOCIATED,
    CHAFA_PIXEL_BGRA8_UNASSOCIATED,
    CHAFA_PIXEL_ARGB8_UNASSOCIATED,
    CHAFA_PIXEL_ABGR8_UNASSOCIATED,

    /* 24 bits per pixel */

    CHAFA_PIXEL_RGB8,
    CHAFA_PIXEL_BGR8,

    CHAFA_PIXEL_MAX
}
ChafaPixelType;
objects.description: Enumeration of pixel formats supported by Chafa, distinguishing premultiplied vs. unassociated alpha and channel order for 32-bit and 24-bit layouts. Used by ChafaCanvas and ChafaSymbolMap to interpret input pixel buffers.
Alignment options for placing an element in an area (start, end, center). Typically combined with tucking to control padding.
Resizing policy when fitting an element into an area: stretch (change aspect), fit (preserve aspect with padding), or shrink-to-fit (fit without enlarging).
Color extraction strategy used when determining representative colors per symbol coverage area: average or median.
Color space selection for color comparison/quantization: fast but imprecise RGB, or perceptually tuned DIN99d.
Dithering mode to use when mapping colors to a limited palette: none, ordered, error diffusion, or noise-based.

Bitflag set controlling sequence/output optimizations, such as reusing SGR attributes and compressing repeated cells. Values can be combined; NONE disables all; ALL enables all bits currently defined.

objects.definition:
typedef enum
{
    CHAFA_CANVAS_MODE_TRUECOLOR,
    CHAFA_CANVAS_MODE_INDEXED_256,
    CHAFA_CANVAS_MODE_INDEXED_240,
    CHAFA_CANVAS_MODE_INDEXED_16,
    CHAFA_CANVAS_MODE_FGBG_BGFG,
    CHAFA_CANVAS_MODE_FGBG,
    CHAFA_CANVAS_MODE_INDEXED_8,
    CHAFA_CANVAS_MODE_INDEXED_16_8,

    CHAFA_CANVAS_MODE_MAX
}
ChafaCanvasMode;
objects.description: Terminal color capability/mode selection for canvas output, ranging from truecolor to various indexed palettes and default fg/bg modes.
How pixel data is rendered or transmitted: approximated via symbols, or sent as terminal-specific pixel protocols (sixels, Kitty, iTerm2).
Passthrough guard wrappers for terminals/multiplexers when emitting control sequences: none, GNU Screen, or tmux.

Bitmask enum of CPU/SIMD features that Chafa can utilize. Values indicate support for MMX, SSE4.1, POPCNT, and AVX2. Used with chafa_get_builtin_features() and chafa_get_supported_features() to query capabilities, and with chafa_describe_features() to render a human-readable description. Semantics beyond flag meanings are not documented here.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaFrame ChafaFrame;
objects.description: Opaque frame object representing an image buffer used by Chafa. The struct is forward-declared here and defined privately elsewhere; it encapsulates pixel data with a specified pixel type, dimensions, and rowstride, and supports reference counting via ref/unref.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaImage ChafaImage;
objects.description: Opaque image handle used by the Chafa library. This header only provides a forward declaration; the struct is defined privately elsewhere. It is reference-counted via chafa_image_ref/unref and can be associated with a ChafaFrame using chafa_image_set_frame. Full layout and destruction details are not exposed here.
Enumeration of parser event kinds produced by the Chafa parser: end-of-input, a single Unicode code point, or a terminal control sequence. Actual values are consumed via ChafaEvent accessors.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaEvent ChafaEvent;
objects.description: Opaque event object emitted by ChafaParser. Carries data corresponding to a ChafaEventType. Only forward-declared here; the layout is private and defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaParser ChafaParser;
objects.description: Opaque parser object that accepts input bytes and produces ChafaEvent instances. Only forward-declared here; the layout is private and defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaPlacement ChafaPlacement;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a placement object used by Chafa to control how an image is positioned (tucked and aligned) within a layout. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the structure is defined elsewhere. Lifetime is managed via ref/unref functions.
Referenced type used as a parameter to construct a ChafaPlacement. It is not defined in this header; definition unknown here and thus omitted per instructions.

Alias of a GLib integer type referenced as parameter to chafa_placement_new. Not defined here; included only if explicitly defined, which it is not. Note: per instructions, referenced but not defined types should be ignored; therefore this entry intentionally contains no definition and should be considered non-applicable.

Enumeration or type used to specify how content is tucked/anchored; referenced by getter/setter but not defined in this header. Per instructions, referenced-only types should be ignored; no definition here.

Enumeration or type used for horizontal/vertical alignment; referenced by getters/setters but not defined in this header. Per instructions, referenced-only types should be ignored; no definition here.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaStreamReader ChafaStreamReader;
objects.description: Opaque stream reader handle for Chafa. The struct is forward-declared only in this header; its internal fields are private. It represents a reference-counted reader bound to a file descriptor, with optional tokenized reading and wait/EOF utilities. Details of lifetime management are via chafa_stream_reader_ref/unref. Full structure definition is not available here.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaStreamWriter ChafaStreamWriter;
objects.description: Opaque stream writer handle used by Chafa to write bytes/text to a file descriptor, optionally buffering and detecting whether the target is a console/tty. This header only provides a forward declaration; the structure is defined privately in the implementation. Lifetime is managed with ref/unref semantics.

objects.definition:
typedef enum
{
    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_NONE        = 0,

    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_SPACE       = (1 <<  0),
    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_SOLID       = (1 <<  1),
    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_STIPPLE     = (1 <<  2),
    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_BLOCK       = (1 <<  3),
    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_BORDER      = (1 <<  4),
    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_DIAGONAL    = (1 <<  5),

    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_QUAD        = (1 <<  7),
    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_HHALF       = (1 <<  8),

    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_HALF        = ((CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_HHALF) | (CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_VHALF)),
    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_INVERTED    = (1 << 10),
    CHAFA_SYMBOL_TAG_BRAILLE     = (1 << 11),

ChafaSymbolTags;
objects.description: Bitmask enum classifying groups and properties of symbols/glyphs in Chafa. Values can be ORed to select sets of symbols (e.g., geometric, braille, alphanumeric). Used as selectors in ChafaSymbolMap.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaSymbolMap ChafaSymbolMap;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a set/map of symbols available to Chafa’s renderer, with APIs to add/remove by tags or Unicode ranges and to manage custom glyph bitmaps. Reference-counted via ref/unref.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaTermDb ChafaTermDb;
objects.description: Opaque handle to the terminal database used by Chafa for detecting and describing terminal capabilities. The actual struct is not defined in this header, indicating it is private/opaque. Lifetime is managed with ref/unref; copy creates a deep or equivalent duplicate; get_default returns a shared default instance.

Enumeration of terminal control sequence identifiers used by Chafa. The specific enumerators are generated from chafa-term-seq-def.h and end with a sentinel CHAFA_TERM_SEQ_MAX. Used to reference, emit, and parse terminal sequences supported by a terminal.
Bitmask flags describing terminal-specific quirks affecting behavior. Currently defines CHAFA_TERM_QUIRK_SIXEL_OVERSHOOT to account for cursor positioning after sixel output.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaTermInfo ChafaTermInfo;
objects.description: Opaque handle describing terminal capabilities, sequences, modes, and quirks for Chafa. Actual structure is private; manage via provided API (new/copy/ref/unref).
Error codes for ChafaTermInfo control-sequence handling and validation, used with the CHAFA_TERM_INFO_ERROR GQuark domain.
Return codes for parsing operations: success, failure, or need more input.

objects.definition: typedef struct ChafaTerm ChafaTerm;
objects.description: Opaque terminal context type for Chafa. This header only forward-declares the struct; its contents are private and defined elsewhere. Instances are created and owned through the chafa_term_* API and represent an I/O and capability-aware handle to a terminal session.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It declares only two functions. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.

No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only defines preprocessor macros for versioning and symbol visibility. Therefore, there are no extractable user-defined types here.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new ChafaCanvasConfig object with default settings. Use this as the starting point to configure canvas conversion parameters before creating or using a canvas.
requirements: Callers receive a newly allocated ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
The returned object is reference-counted; callers must eventually release it (e.g., with chafa_canvas_config_unref).
Thread-safety/initialization guarantees are unknown.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_copy
functions.description: Creates a copy of an existing ChafaCanvasConfig. Useful for duplicating configuration state before making modifications.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returns a new reference-counted ChafaCanvasConfig; callers must unref it when done.
Exact copy semantics for any referenced sub-objects (deep vs. shallow) are unknown.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_ref
functions.description: Increments the reference count of the given ChafaCanvasConfig to claim a new reference.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Every successful chafa_canvas_config_ref call must be balanced with a corresponding chafa_canvas_config_unref.
Behavior is undefined if called on an already finalized or invalid object.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_unref
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of the given ChafaCanvasConfig. When the count reaches zero, the object is finalized and its resources are freed.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer or NULL handling is unspecified (pass a valid pointer).
After the reference count reaches zero, the object must not be accessed again.
Every owned reference must be released exactly once to avoid leaks or double-frees.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_geometry
functions.description: Retrieves the configured output canvas geometry in character cells (width and height).
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
width_out and height_out should be valid, writable pointers; whether NULL is allowed is unspecified—pass non-NULL to be safe.
Units and valid range of the returned values are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_geometry
functions.signature: void chafa_canvas_config_set_geometry (ChafaCanvasConfig *config, gint width, gint height);
functions.description: Sets the output canvas geometry in character cells (width and height).
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Valid ranges/limits for width and height are unspecified (non-negative, non-zero expectations are not stated).
Effect on existing dependent settings (e.g., cell geometry) is unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_cell_geometry
functions.description: Retrieves the configured size of a single character cell in pixels (cell width and height).
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
cell_width_out and cell_height_out should be valid, writable pointers; whether NULL is allowed is unspecified—pass non-NULL to be safe.
Units and valid range are not explicitly documented.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_cell_geometry
functions.signature: void chafa_canvas_config_set_cell_geometry (ChafaCanvasConfig *config, gint cell_width, gint cell_height);
functions.description: Sets the pixel dimensions of a single character cell used during rendering.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Valid ranges/limits for cell_width and cell_height are unspecified.
Relationship with overall canvas geometry is unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_canvas_mode
functions.description: Returns the current canvas mode, which selects the terminal/canvas representation strategy.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned value is a ChafaCanvasMode enum; exact set of modes is defined elsewhere.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_canvas_mode
functions.description: Sets the canvas mode that controls how content is represented on the terminal/canvas.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
mode must be a valid ChafaCanvasMode value; accepted values and constraints are defined elsewhere.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_color_extractor
functions.description: Returns the color extractor strategy used to derive colors from source images.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned value is a ChafaColorExtractor enum; available options are defined elsewhere.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_color_extractor
functions.description: Sets the color extraction strategy used during conversion.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
color_extractor must be a valid ChafaColorExtractor value.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_color_space
functions.description: Returns the color space used for color computations during rendering.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned value is a ChafaColorSpace enum.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_color_space
functions.description: Sets the color space used for color computations.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
color_space must be a valid ChafaColorSpace value.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_peek_symbol_map
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the symbol map used for drawing (foreground/content symbols). The pointer is const and typically represents internal configuration state.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned pointer must not be modified. Whether the caller owns a reference or may retain the pointer beyond immediate use is unspecified; treat as a non-owning, borrowed pointer.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_symbol_map
functions.description: Sets the symbol map used for drawing (the set of characters/glyphs for content).
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
symbol_map must be a valid ChafaSymbolMap pointer.
Ownership/reference semantics are unspecified (whether the config copies or refs the map). Ensure symbol_map remains valid according to library expectations.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_peek_fill_symbol_map
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the symbol map used for filling/background-like operations. The pointer is const and likely refers to internal state.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned pointer must not be modified. Treat as non-owning; exact lifetime/ownership semantics are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_fill_symbol_map
functions.description: Sets the symbol map used for fill/background usage.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
fill_symbol_map must be a valid ChafaSymbolMap pointer.
Ownership/reference semantics are unspecified (copy vs. reference).

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_transparency_threshold
functions.description: Returns the alpha/transparency threshold used to treat pixels as transparent during rendering.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned range/units are not documented (commonly 0.0–1.0, but unspecified here).

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_transparency_threshold
functions.description: Sets the alpha/transparency threshold used to decide when pixels are considered transparent.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Valid range for alpha_threshold is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_fg_color
functions.description: Returns the foreground color as a packed RGB integer.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Exact packing format and valid range are not documented here (likely 0xRRGGBB, but unspecified).

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_fg_color
functions.description: Sets the foreground color using a packed RGB integer.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Packing format and valid range for fg_color_packed_rgb are unspecified in this header.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_bg_color
functions.description: Returns the background color as a packed RGB integer.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Exact packing format and range are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_bg_color
functions.description: Sets the background color using a packed RGB integer.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Packing format and valid range for bg_color_packed_rgb are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_work_factor
functions.description: Returns the work factor controlling effort/quality trade-offs in processing.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Scale and valid range of the work factor are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_work_factor
functions.description: Sets the work factor to adjust effort/quality trade-offs.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Valid range and effects of work_factor are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_preprocessing_enabled
functions.description: Returns whether preprocessing steps are enabled during conversion.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_preprocessing_enabled
functions.description: Enables or disables preprocessing steps for conversion.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_dither_mode
functions.description: Returns the dithering mode used during color/brightness quantization.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned value is a ChafaDitherMode enum.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_dither_mode
functions.description: Sets the dithering mode used during rendering.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
dither_mode must be a valid ChafaDitherMode value.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_dither_grain_size
functions.description: Retrieves the grain size used for dithering (width and height).
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
width_out and height_out should be valid, writable pointers; whether NULL is allowed is unspecified—pass non-NULL to be safe.
Valid range/units are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_dither_grain_size
functions.signature: void chafa_canvas_config_set_dither_grain_size (ChafaCanvasConfig *config, gint width, gint height);
functions.description: Sets the grain size for dithering (width and height).
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Valid ranges for width and height are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_dither_intensity
functions.description: Returns the dithering intensity factor.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Valid range/scale are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_dither_intensity
functions.description: Sets the dithering intensity factor.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Valid range/scale for intensity are unspecified.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_pixel_mode
functions.description: Returns the pixel mode determining how pixels are represented (e.g., block/half-block based).
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned value is a ChafaPixelMode enum.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_pixel_mode
functions.description: Sets the pixel mode controlling pixel representation on the canvas.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
pixel_mode must be a valid ChafaPixelMode value.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_optimizations
functions.description: Returns the set of enabled optimizations flags affecting performance/quality trade-offs.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned value is a ChafaOptimizations flag set; exact bits/meanings are defined elsewhere.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_optimizations
functions.description: Sets optimization flags to adjust performance/quality trade-offs.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
optimizations must be a valid combination of ChafaOptimizations flags.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_fg_only_enabled
functions.description: Returns whether foreground-only rendering is enabled.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_fg_only_enabled
functions.description: Enables or disables foreground-only rendering.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_get_passthrough
functions.description: Returns the passthrough mode controlling how certain sequences or data are emitted without processing.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
Returned value is a ChafaPassthrough enum.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_config_set_passthrough
functions.description: Sets the passthrough mode controlling emission of certain data without processing.
requirements: config must be a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig pointer.
passthrough must be a valid ChafaPassthrough value.

functions.name: chafa_canvas_new
functions.description: Creates a new ChafaCanvas using the provided configuration. Use this as the primary constructor before drawing or printing. Returns a newly created canvas handle or possibly NULL on failure (return semantics not documented here).
requirements: config must point to a valid, initialized ChafaCanvasConfig structure
The returned ChafaCanvas must be managed via chafa_canvas_ref()/chafa_canvas_unref() if reference counting is used by the caller (exact ownership rules unknown)

functions.name: chafa_canvas_new_similar
functions.description: Creates a new ChafaCanvas similar to the given one (likely copying configuration and/or dimensions). Useful for duplicating settings from an existing canvas. Exact similarities are not documented here.
requirements: orig must be a valid ChafaCanvas previously created by the API
The returned ChafaCanvas is a distinct object; manage its lifetime separately (ownership specifics unknown)

functions.name: chafa_canvas_ref
functions.description: Increases the reference count of the given canvas. Call to retain a canvas across API boundaries or longer lifetimes.
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas pointer obtained from this API
Each successful chafa_canvas_ref() should be balanced with a later chafa_canvas_unref()

functions.name: chafa_canvas_unref
functions.description: Decreases the reference count of the given canvas, potentially freeing it when the count reaches zero.
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas pointer obtained from this API
Do not use the canvas after its final unref drops the last reference
Calls to chafa_canvas_unref() must be balanced with prior ownership/ref acquisitions

functions.name: chafa_canvas_peek_config
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the canvas' current configuration for inspection. The returned pointer is const and likely owned by the canvas; do not modify or free it.
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas
The returned ChafaCanvasConfig pointer must not be modified or freed by the caller
The configuration pointer may become invalid if the canvas is destroyed; do not use it after the canvas' lifetime ends

functions.name: chafa_canvas_set_placement
functions.description: Sets placement parameters on the canvas, likely controlling output alignment or positioning. Exact semantics depend on ChafaPlacement and are not detailed here.
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas
placement must point to a valid ChafaPlacement structure initialized as required by its API (exact fields/constraints unknown)

functions.name: chafa_canvas_draw_all_pixels
functions.signature: void chafa_canvas_draw_all_pixels (ChafaCanvas *canvas, ChafaPixelType src_pixel_type, const guint8 *src_pixels, gint src_width, gint src_height, gint src_rowstride);
functions.description: Draws pixel data into the canvas from a raw source buffer covering the full image. Use to render an image of given dimensions and pixel format onto the canvas.
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas
src_pixel_type must be a valid ChafaPixelType value supported by the library
src_pixels must point to a buffer large enough for the specified dimensions and rowstride
src_width and src_height should describe the image dimensions; they must be non-negative
src_rowstride should be the number of bytes between successive rows in src_pixels; it must be large enough to cover each row for the chosen pixel type (exact minimum not specified)

functions.name: chafa_canvas_print
functions.description: Generates a terminal-ready representation of the canvas as a single GString, using terminal capability information. Use this to print the entire canvas in one block.
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas
term_info must be a valid ChafaTermInfo describing the target terminal's capabilities
The returned GString is heap-allocated; freeing/ownership semantics are not specified here (likely free with g_string_free, but not guaranteed)

functions.name: chafa_canvas_print_rows
functions.description: Produces the canvas output split into multiple rows, returning them as an array of GString pointers and the array length. Useful for row-wise emission to a terminal.
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas
term_info must be a valid ChafaTermInfo
array_out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive an array of GString* (ownership and freeing protocol not specified)
array_len_out must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of rows

functions.name: chafa_canvas_print_rows_strv
functions.description: Produces the canvas output split into rows as a NULL-terminated array of C strings (strv). Useful when plain UTF-8 strings are preferred over GString objects. Exact ownership and freeing rules are not specified here.
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas
term_info must be a valid ChafaTermInfo
The returned gchar** is a NULL-terminated vector of strings; caller must handle memory according to library conventions (specifics unknown)

functions.name: chafa_canvas_get_char_at
functions.signature: gunichar chafa_canvas_get_char_at (ChafaCanvas *canvas, gint x, gint y);
functions.description: Returns the Unicode character currently stored at the given canvas cell coordinates. Useful for inspecting the rendered character grid.
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas
x and y should denote valid coordinates within the canvas bounds (exact bounds and behavior on out-of-range are not documented)

functions.name: chafa_canvas_set_char_at
functions.signature: gint chafa_canvas_set_char_at (ChafaCanvas *canvas, gint x, gint y, gunichar c);
functions.description: Sets the Unicode character at the specified canvas cell coordinates. Returns an integer status code; exact return semantics are not documented here (nonzero/zero unknown).
requirements: canvas must be a valid ChafaCanvas
x and y should be within the canvas bounds (exact bounds and error behavior unknown)

import random
import struct
from typing import Tuple

# Target data type: raw pixel buffer
# The fuzz stubs request a std::string (FUZZ_PARAM_STR) that is used as the backing
# raw pixel buffer for various Chafa entry points. They also compute external
# parameters: pixel format (implies bytes-per-pixel), width, height, and rowstride.
# Our job is to return an initial bytes value that is likely valid for many such
# choices and can exercise different behaviors while remaining within 4096 bytes.
#
# Strategy
# - Construct a raw pixel buffer containing multiple structured regions of data
#   to be reused for different bpp/stride/size combinations chosen by the fuzzer.
# - Include gradients, solid color runs, alpha ramps, checkerboards, and noise.
# - Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - The buffer is generic (not specific to one geometry); the stubs slice/resize
#   it to the exact required size. By making the data rich and patterned, we
#   encourage diverse rendering paths for both RGB8 and RGBA8 inputs.
#
# Composition (in order):
# 1) Header tag (not interpreted by target, but adds variability)
# 2) Repeating gradient blocks for 3 bpp and 4 bpp assumptions
# 3) Checkerboard region
# 4) Alpha ramp region (useful for RGBA paths)
# 5) Low-entropy runs (all zeros, all 0xFF)
# 6) Pseudo-random noise tail
#
# All concatenated to produce a byte string <= 2048 bytes so it also fits the
# stricter limits used by the stubs.

MAX_TOTAL = 2048  # Stay within stub limits comfortably


def _grad_block(width: int, height: int, bpp: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for y in range(height):
        for x in range(width):
            r = (x * 255) // max(1, width - 1)
            g = (y * 255) // max(1, height - 1)
            b = ((x + y) * 255) // max(1, width + height - 2)
            if bpp == 3:
                out.extend((r, g, b))
            else:
                a = (255 if ((x ^ y) & 1) == 0 else 128)
                out.extend((r, g, b, a))
    return bytes(out)


def _checker_block(width: int, height: int, bpp: int, size: int = 2) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for y in range(height):
        for x in range(width):
            on = ((x // size) + (y // size)) & 1
            r, g, b = (0xE0, 0x20, 0x20) if on else (0x20, 0xE0, 0x20)
            if bpp == 3:
                out.extend((r, g, b))
            else:
                a = 255 if on else 0
                out.extend((r, g, b, a))
    return bytes(out)


def _alpha_ramp(width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
    # RGBA ramp left->right alpha, color varies with y
    out = bytearray()
    for y in range(height):
        for x in range(width):
            a = (x * 255) // max(1, width - 1)
            r = (y * 255) // max(1, height - 1)
            g = 255 - r
            b = (r + g) // 4
            out.extend((r, g, b, a))
    return bytes(out)


def _runs(length: int, pattern: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([pattern & 0xFF]) * length


def _noise(length: int, rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return rnd.randbytes(length)


def _pack_le_u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide block sizes (small to keep total under MAX_TOTAL)
    # Use a mix of sizes so various rowstride computations in the stubs will
    # slice different amounts from this buffer.
    w1, h1 = rnd.randint(4, 16), rnd.randint(4, 16)   # gradient 3bpp
    w2, h2 = rnd.randint(4, 16), rnd.randint(4, 16)   # gradient 4bpp
    w3, h3 = rnd.randint(4, 12), rnd.randint(4, 12)   # checker 3/4bpp alt
    w4, h4 = rnd.randint(8, 16), rnd.randint(2, 8)    # alpha ramp rgba

    # Build sections
    sections = []
    # Simple header for variety
    header = b'CHAF' + _pack_le_u32(w1 << 16 | h1) + _pack_le_u32(seed)
    sections.append(header)

    # Gradient RGB
    grad_rgb = _grad_block(w1, h1, 3)
    sections.append(grad_rgb)

    # Gradient RGBA
    grad_rgba = _grad_block(w2, h2, 4)
    sections.append(grad_rgba)

    # Checkerboard: alternate bpp selection based on seed
    if rnd.getrandbits(1):
        chk = _checker_block(w3, h3, 3)
    else:
        chk = _checker_block(w3, h3, 4)
    sections.append(chk)

    # Alpha ramp (RGBA)
    sections.append(_alpha_ramp(w4, h4))

    # Low entropy runs
    sections.append(_runs(rnd.randint(16, 64), 0x00))
    sections.append(_runs(rnd.randint(16, 64), 0xFF))

    # Noise tail sized to fill up to a randomized target below MAX_TOTAL
    body = b''.join(sections)
    # Choose target size between len(body)+64 and min(MAX_TOTAL, len(body)+512)
    min_target = min(MAX_TOTAL, len(body) + 64)
    max_target = min(MAX_TOTAL, len(body) + 512)
    target = rnd.randint(min_target, max_target) if max_target > min_target else min_target
    if target < len(body):
        target = len(body)
    noise_len = max(0, target - len(body))
    body += _noise(noise_len, rnd)

    # Ensure final size <= MAX_TOTAL
    if len(body) > MAX_TOTAL:
        body = body[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return body

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for terminal byte stream inputs targeting chafa_parser_push_data and
# chafa_term_info_parse_seq(_varargs). We focus on creating valid and interesting
# terminal-like byte streams: UTF-8 text, ANSI/CSI sequences with varying args,
# OSC sequences, DCS/SIXEL stubs, mouse reports, DEC private modes, and mixtures.

# Notes
# - Must return bytes <= 4096.
# - Deterministic with seed, but varied each call.
# - Avoid post-mutation; construct valid sequences directly.

CSI = "\x1b[".encode()
OSC = "\x1b]".encode()
ST  = "\x1b\\".encode()   # String Terminator
BEL = b"\x07"
ESC = b"\x1b"
DCS = b"\x1bP"
SOS = b"\x1bX"  # rarely used, but valid string introducer
PM  = b"\x1b^"
APC = b"\x1b_"

# Helpers to build sequences

def _rand_utf8_text(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix printable ASCII, multibyte UTF-8, and spaces/newlines
    out = bytearray()
    # Ensure at least a couple code points
    n = r.randint(1, max(1, max_len // 2))
    for _ in range(n):
        t = r.random()
        if t < 0.6:
            # printable ASCII 0x20-0x7E
            out.append(r.randint(0x20, 0x7E))
        elif t < 0.8:
            # whitespace/control like tab/newline/carriage return
            out.extend(r.choice([b"\n", b"\r", b"\t", b" "]))
        else:
            # Multibyte UTF-8: pick valid Unicode and encode
            # Choose ranges that are commonly supported in terminals
            cp_ranges = [
                (0x00A0, 0x00FF),   # Latin-1 supplement
                (0x2500, 0x257F),   # Box drawing
                (0x2580, 0x259F),   # Block elements
                (0x1F300, 0x1F64F), # Emojis (may be dropped but valid UTF-8)
                (0x2800, 0x28FF),   # Braille patterns
            ]
            lo, hi = r.choice(cp_ranges)
            cp = r.randint(lo, hi)
            out.extend(chr(cp).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
        if len(out) >= max_len:
            break
    return bytes(out[:max_len])


def _csi_params(r: random.Random, max_params: int = 8, allow_priv: bool = True) -> bytes:
    # Generate 0..max_params integers separated by ; including private mode prefix '?'
    parts: List[str] = []
    n = r.randint(0, max_params)
    for _ in range(n):
        # Mix empty (for omitted), small, and larger values
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.15:
            parts.append("")  # omitted value
        elif choice < 0.8:
            parts.append(str(r.randint(0, 255)))
        else:
            parts.append(str(r.randint(256, 9999)))
    prefix = "?" if (allow_priv and r.random() < 0.25) else ""
    return (prefix + ";".join(parts)).encode()


def _make_csi(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # A selection of common final bytes
    finals = [
        b"A", b"B", b"C", b"D",           # CUU/CUD/CUF/CUB
        b"H", b"f",                        # CUP/HVP
        b"J", b"K",                        # ED/EL
        b"m",                              # SGR
        b"n",                              # DSR
        b"s", b"u",                        # save/restore cursor
        b"r",                              # DECSTBM
        b"@", b"P", b"X", b"L", b"M",      # ICH/DCH/ECH/IL/DL
        b"t",                              # window ops
    ]
    intermed = b""  # could add ' ' to '/'
    params = _csi_params(r)
    return CSI + params + intermed + r.choice(finals)


def _make_osc(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # OSC Ps ; Pt ST or BEL. Common Ps: 0,1,2 (icon/title), 4 (palette), 52 (clipboard)
    ps = str(r.choice([0, 1, 2, 4, 10, 11, 12, 52, 104, 112]))
    # Payload: printable UTF-8 text, possibly with semicolons
    text_len = r.randint(0, 60)
    payload = _rand_utf8_text(r, text_len).replace(b"\x07", b"")
    # For OSC 52 (clipboard), format: 52; c; <base64> usually; we just put sane text
    sep_payload = payload.replace(b";", b":")
    body = ps.encode() + b";" + sep_payload
    terminator = BEL if r.random() < 0.5 else ST
    return OSC + body + terminator


def _make_dcs_sixel_stub(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # DCS ... ST, optionally resembling SIXEL intro "q" and some data
    # We'll keep short, valid-terminating string
    content = bytearray()
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        content.extend(b"0;0;q")  # rudimentary sixel header
        # Add a few printable sixel chars ("?-~") and data separators '#', '$', '-'
        for _ in range(r.randint(5, 40)):
            content.append(r.choice(list(b"#$-?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~")))
    else:
        # Generic DCS payload
        content.extend(_rand_utf8_text(r, r.randint(5, 60)))
    return DCS + bytes(content) + ST


def _make_mouse_report(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # X10 mouse report: ESC [ M Cb Cx Cy with coords offset 32
    cb = 32 + r.randint(0, 255) % 64
    cx = 32 + (r.randint(1, 200) % 223)
    cy = 32 + (r.randint(1, 100) % 223)
    return CSI + b"M" + bytes([cb, cx, cy])


def _make_dec_private_mode(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # DECSET/DECRST: CSI ? Pm h/l
    params = _csi_params(r, allow_priv=True)
    final = b"h" if r.random() < 0.5 else b"l"
    return CSI + params if params.startswith(b"?") else CSI + b"?" + params + final


def _make_csi_sgr_complex(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a rich SGR with many parameters
    parts: List[str] = []
    base = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27, 29]
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 12)):
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(str(r.choice(base)))
        else:
            # 38/48 extended colors: 38;5;idx or 38;2;r;g;b
            if r.random() < 0.5:
                idx = r.randint(0, 255)
                parts.extend(["38", "5", str(idx)])
            else:
                rgb = [str(r.randint(0, 255)) for _ in range(3)]
                parts.extend(["38", "2", *rgb])
    return CSI + ";".join(parts).encode() + b"m"


def _make_csi_cursor_position(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    row = r.randint(1, 200)

        else:

        if not piece:

# Target data type: binary data
# The fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR for payloads that are written/read via stream readers/writers and terminal write APIs.
# Valid/interesting inputs here are arbitrary bytes, but we bias towards:
# - Mixtures of text-like and binary bytes
# - Inclusion of common token separators (\n, \r\n, NUL, tabs) to exercise tokenization paths
# - Varied lengths, including empty, small, and moderate sizes (cap at <= 4096)
# - Repeated patterns and random chunks
# - UTF-8-like sequences as well as invalid UTF-8 to ensure opaque handling
#
# The stubs also use FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for sizing and token separator selection; those are generated by the fuzzer, not by us.
# Our role is to provide the initial seed buffer that will be used primarily by FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

CONTROL_SEQS: List[bytes] = [
    b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\t", b"\x00", b" ", b",", b";", b"|",
]

TEXT_SNIPPETS: List[bytes] = [
    b"Hello, Chafa!\n",
    b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\n",
    b"\x1b[31mRED\x1b[0m \x1b[32mGREEN\x1b[0m\n",  # ANSI-like sequences
    b"Token1,Token2;Token3|End\n",
    b"UTF-8: \xe2\x98\x83 \xf0\x9f\x8d\x8e\n",  # snowman, apple
]

BINARY_CHUNKS: List[bytes] = [
    bytes(range(0, 64)),                 # ascending bytes
    bytes(range(255, 255-64, -1)),       # descending bytes
    b"\x00" * 32,                        # NUL run
    b"\xff" * 32,                        # 0xFF run
    b"\x00\xff" * 16,                   # alternating
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


essential_separators = [b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\x00"]

def _build_payload(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Start with a header that mixes text and binary to exercise both paths
    header_choices = [
        rng.choice(TEXT_SNIPPETS),
        rng.choice(BINARY_CHUNKS),
        _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(8, 64)),
    ]
    parts.append(rng.choice(header_choices))

    # Insert common separators multiple times to create tokens for the reader with tokenizer
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        parts.append(rng.choice(CONTROL_SEQS))
        # Follow by short random or text snippet
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 32)))
        else:
            parts.append(rng.choice(TEXT_SNIPPETS))

    # Optionally include an ANSI-like control sequence burst to test terminal write functions
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        # CSI sequences with parameters
        params = [str(rng.randint(0, 255)).encode() for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5))]
        csi = b"\x1b[" + b";".join(params) + b"m"
        parts.append(csi)
        parts.append(b"Styled text\n")

    # Add a few patterned and random blocks
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.3:
            parts.append(rng.choice(BINARY_CHUNKS))
        elif choice < 0.6:
            # Repeated small token to encourage token-splitting
            token = rng.choice([b"\n", b";", b",", b"|", b"\x00"])  # likely separators
            parts.append(token * rng.randint(1, 16))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(16, 128)))

    # Ensure at least one of each essential separator exists to maximize tokenization coverage
    for sep in essential_separators:
        if not any(sep in chunk for chunk in parts if isinstance(chunk, (bytes, bytearray))):
            parts.append(sep)

    # Optionally end with CRLF or NUL to close a token cleanly
    parts.append(rng.choice([b"\r\n", b"\n", b"\x00"]))

    # Concatenate and trim/pad to target_len
    out = b"".join(parts)
    if target_len <= 0:
        return b""
    if len(out) > target_len:
        return out[:target_len]
    # If shorter, append random to reach target
    if len(out) < target_len:
        out += _rand_bytes(rng, target_len - len(out))
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide total length with a distribution favoring small to medium payloads, but sometimes larger
    bucket = rng.random()
    if bucket < 0.2:
        total_len = rng.randint(0, 32)            # include empty to small
    elif bucket < 0.7:
        total_len = rng.randint(64, 512)          # common medium sizes
    elif bucket < 0.95:
        total_len = rng.randint(513, 2048)        # larger
    else:
        total_len = rng.randint(2049, MAX_TOTAL)  # rare max-size cases

    total_len = min(total_len, MAX_TOTAL)

    # Build a composite payload which will seed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
    # We structure it as blocks separated by random separators to give the fuzzer
    # a variety of distinct substrings to draw from.
    n_blocks = rng.randint(2, 6)
    block_target = max(1, total_len // n_blocks)
    blocks: List[bytes] = []
    for i in range(n_blocks):
        # Slightly vary block sizes
        target = block_target + rng.randint(-block_target // 2, block_target // 2)
        target = max(0, target)
        blocks.append(_build_payload(rng, target))
        # Insert a separator between blocks to create natural token boundaries
        if i != n_blocks - 1:
            blocks.append(rng.choice(CONTROL_SEQS))

    out = b"".join(blocks)
    if len(out) > total_len:
        out = out[:total_len]
    elif len(out) < total_len:
        out += _rand_bytes(rng, total_len - len(out))

    return out

import random
from typing import List

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate arbitrary binary including potential control/separator-like bytes
    # Mix ranges to cover edge cases
    chunks: List[int] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        mode = r.randrange(6)
        if mode == 0:
            # ASCII letters/digits
            chunks.append(r.choice(list(range(0x30, 0x3A)) + list(range(0x41, 0x5B)) + list(range(0x61, 0x7B))))
        elif mode == 1:
            # Whitespace/control
            chunks.append(r.choice([0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0D]))
        elif mode == 2:
            # Punctuation that often appears in delimiters
            chunks.append(r.choice(list(map(ord, ",;:|/\\-_=+*#@[]{}()<>"))))
        elif mode == 3:
            # High bytes
            chunks.append(r.randrange(0x80, 0x100))
        elif mode == 4:
            # Common token-like sequences embedded
            # We'll add one byte from a chosen sequence to keep randomization
            seqs = [b"\r\n", b"\n", b"\r", b"--", b"::", b"||", b"\x1b]1337;", b"\x1bPq", b"\0"]
            s = r.choice(seqs)
            chunks.append(s[r.randrange(len(s))])
        else:
            chunks.append(r.randrange(256))
    return bytes(chunks)

# We need to feed two FUZZ_PARAM_STR occurrences: one for pipe payload (data), one for separator (sep). 
# Goal: produce a buffer that, when split by the harness, yields interesting combinations:
# - Non-empty data for the pipe so read() returns some bytes, sometimes including separator to test token splits.
# - A plausible, non-empty separator including common delimiters and binary cases.
# The harness constrains sep_len to 1..sep.size(), so we only need to ensure sep has size > 0.


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Strategy: Build a self-describing container so the fuzzer infra can split into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    # Many harnesses consume the provided bytes sequentially. We'll craft two length-prefixed blobs:
    # [u16 data_len][data][u16 sep_len][sep]
    # Keep total <= 4096

    # Choose lengths with bias toward small and also some larger cases
    def pick_len(max_len: int) -> int:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.4:
            return r.randrange(0, min(64, max_len) + 1)
        if choice < 0.8:
            return r.randrange(1, min(512, max_len) + 1)
        return r.randrange(1, max_len + 1)

    max_total = 4096

    # Reserve 4 bytes for two u16 lengths
    budget = max_total - 4

    # Separator must be at least 1 byte to make tokenizer active when mode bit enables it.
    # We'll bias to small lengths but allow some larger to test scanning.
    sep_len = max(1, pick_len(min(256, budget // 3)))

    # Data length gets the remaining budget share
    data_len = max(0, pick_len(min(2048, budget - sep_len)))

    # Generate data payload: include multiple occurrences of the separator patterns sometimes
    data = _rand_bytes(r, data_len)

    # Generate a separator with structure: choose from a curated set or random binary
    common_seps = [
        b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\r", b"||", b"::", b"--", b",", b";", b"\x00", b"\x1f", b"\x1b]1337;",
        b"\x1bPq", b"END", b"TOKEN", b"::END::"
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        base = r.choice(common_seps)
        # Expand or truncate to sep_len while keeping some recognizable prefix
        if len(base) >= sep_len:
            sep = base[:sep_len]
        else:
            # Repeat and mix with random bytes to reach sep_len
            needed = sep_len - len(base)
            sep = base + _rand_bytes(r, needed)
    else:
        sep = _rand_bytes(r, sep_len)

    # Occasionally ensure the data contains the separator to exercise token splitting
    if data_len > 0 and r.random() < 0.75:
        insert_times = 1 + (0 if data_len < 32 else r.randrange(0, 3))
        for _ in range(insert_times):
            if len(sep) == 0:
                break
            pos = r.randrange(0, max(1, len(data)))
            # Insert sep at position pos, but cap total size
            new_len = len(data) + len(sep)
            if new_len > 2048:  # keep data not too large
                break
            data = data[:pos] + sep + data[pos:]

    # Truncate if we exceeded budget
    total_needed = 4 + len(data) + len(sep)
    if total_needed > 4096:
        # Prefer truncating data, keep separator intact and non-empty
        to_trim = total_needed - 4096
        if to_trim > 0 and len(data) > to_trim:
            data = data[:-to_trim]
        else:
            data = data[:max(0, len(data) - to_trim)]
        total_needed = 4 + len(data) + len(sep)
        if total_needed > 4096 and len(sep) > 1:
            sep = sep[:max(1, len(sep) - (total_needed - 4096))]

    # Build the buffer: u16 lengths little-endian followed by blobs
    def u16le(n: int) -> bytes:
        return bytes((n & 0xFF, (n >> 8) & 0xFF))

    out = bytearray()
    out += u16le(len(data))
    out += data
    out += u16le(len(sep))
    out += sep

    return bytes(out)

from typing import List

# Data type: UTF-8 text (NUL-terminated in C usage). We will generate bytes that
# are valid UTF-8 and often printable, sometimes including edge cases like
# multibyte Unicode, ANSI escape sequences, and embedded NUL terminators are NOT
# allowed here because FUZZ_PARAM_STR expects a std::string (which can contain NULs),
# but for exercising printf %s safely, we avoid embedded NUL so the visible part
# is interesting. We also keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

# This generator returns a single buffer used by the harness to source multiple
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We pack multiple candidate strings separated by newlines
# so that consumers that slice or read chunks get varied content. Newlines are
# safe for printf cases in stubs and allow multi-line messages.

UNICODE_BLOCKS = [
    # Common Latin
    (0x0020, 0x007E),  # printable ASCII
    (0x00A0, 0x00FF),  # Latin-1 Supplement (excluding control)
    # Box drawing and block elements for terminals
    (0x2500, 0x257F),  # Box Drawing
    (0x2580, 0x259F),  # Block Elements
    (0x2460, 0x24FF),  # Enclosed Alphanumerics
    # Emoji subset for UTF-8 variety
    (0x1F600, 0x1F64F),  # Emoticons
]

ANSI_ESCAPES = [
    "\x1b[0m", "\x1b[1m", "\x1b[3m", "\x1b[4m", "\x1b[7m",
    "\x1b[31m", "\x1b[32m", "\x1b[33m", "\x1b[34m", "\x1b[35m", "\x1b[36m",
    "\x1b[39m", "\x1b[49m",
]

SAFE_NAMES = [
    "xterm-256color", "screen", "tmux", "vt100", "kitty", "iTerm2",
    "ansi", "dumb", "linux", "rxvt-unicode",
]

LITERALS = [
    "Hello, world!",
    "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
    "CAFÉ – déjà vu — naïve façade.",
    "Box: ┌─┬─┐\n│ ░│█ │\n└─┴─┘",
    "Blocks: ▀▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█ ▉▊▋▌▍▎▏",
    "Braille: ⠁⠃⠇⠟⠿",
]


def _rand_unicode_char(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    block = rng.choice(UNICODE_BLOCKS)
    cp = rng.randint(block[0], block[1])
    # Avoid surrogate halves and non-characters
    if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
        cp = 0xE000
    if 0xFDD0 <= cp <= 0xFDEF or (cp & 0xFFFE) == 0xFFFE:
        cp = 0x25A1  # white square as fallback
    try:
        return chr(cp)
    except ValueError:
        return "?"


def _rand_printable_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))


def _make_utf8_string(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII, Unicode, and optional ANSI escapes.
    parts: List[str] = []
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target_len:
        choice = rng.random()
        remaining = target_len - sum(len(p) for p in parts)
        if choice < 0.5:
            chunk = _rand_printable_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, max(1, min(16, remaining))))
        elif choice < 0.85:
            # Unicode chunk
            count = rng.randint(1, max(1, min(8, remaining)))
            chunk = ''.join(_rand_unicode_char(rng) for _ in range(count))
        else:
            chunk = rng.choice(ANSI_ESCAPES)
        parts.append(chunk)
        # Occasionally insert whitespace/newline to simulate paragraphs
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            parts.append("\n")
    s = ''.join(parts)
    # Trim to exact or less than target_len to avoid overly long outputs
    if len(s) > target_len:
        s = s[:target_len]
    # Ensure it is valid UTF-8 by encoding; replace unlikely invalids defensively
    s = s.encode('utf-8', 'strict').decode('utf-8', 'strict')
    return s


def _make_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(SAFE_NAMES)
    # Construct a plausible TERM-like name
    base = rng.choice(["xterm", "screen", "tmux", "vt", "linux", "rxvt", "alacritty"]) \
        + ("-" + str(rng.choice([16, 88, 256, 240])) + "color" if rng.random() < 0.7 else "")
    suffix = rng.choice(["", "+truecolor", "+sixel", "+kitty"]) if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""
    return base + suffix


def _compose_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # We will build multiple lines, each a separate candidate string segment the fuzzer can use:
    # 1) A medium message for term_print/err
    # 2) A short string, a long string, and a unicode-heavy string for stream_writer_print
    # 3) A terminal name candidate (possibly empty to exercise NULL in stub path)
    # 4) Some pure ANSI sequences line
    segments: List[str] = []

    # Segment 1: medium message
    segments.append(_make_utf8_string(rng, rng.randint(32, 128)))

    # Segment 2: short and long messages
    segments.append(_make_utf8_string(rng, rng.randint(1, 24)))
    segments.append(_make_utf8_string(rng, rng.randint(128, 512)))

    # Segment 3: unicode-heavy
    uni = ''.join(_rand_unicode_char(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(16, 64)))
    segments.append(uni)

    # Segment 4: terminal name
    segments.append(_make_name(rng))

    # Segment 5: literals pool to hit specific code paths
    segments.extend(rng.sample(LITERALS, k=rng.randint(1, min(3, len(LITERALS)))))

    # Segment 6: pure ANSI line for terminals
    segments.append(''.join(rng.choices(ANSI_ESCAPES, k=rng.randint(2, 6))))

    # Join with newlines. Avoid trailing NUL; callers using %s will stop at NUL otherwise.
    blob = ('\n'.join(segments) + '\n').encode('utf-8')

    # Ensure <= 4096 bytes
    return blob[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _compose_blob(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for Chafa selector expression strings
# The fuzzer stub passes our buffer to FUZZ_PARAM_STR(), expecting a NUL-terminated UTF-8 string
# with Chafa selector syntax for symbol categories and ranges.
# We aim to produce valid and interesting combinations that exercise:
# - Tag inclusion/exclusion
# - Unicode ranges (BMP and beyond)
# - Shorthand groups and combinations
# - Whitespace variations and comma/semicolon separated lists
# - Nested parentheses and precedence with + / - operators
# The exact grammar is not public here, but Chafa selectors generally accept constructs like:
#   tag:block,tag:braille
#   +block -ugly +braille
#   range:U+2580-259F
#   U+2800-28FF
#   ascii, alnum, geometric, technical, braille, blocks, sextant, octant, wedge, stipple, border, dot, diagonal
#   modifiers like wide, narrow, ambiguous, legacy, extra
# We therefore synthesize expressions from these tokens using operators and separators.

TAGS = [
    "space", "solid", "stipple", "block", "border", "diagonal", "dot", "quad",
    "hhalf", "vhalf", "braille", "technical", "geometric", "ascii",
    "alpha", "digit", "alnum", "narrow", "wide", "ambiguous", "ugly",
    "legacy", "sextant", "wedge", "latin", "imported", "octant", "extra"
]

# Some predefined, commonly useful groups/aliases seen in docs and typical usage
ALIASES = [
    "ascii", "alnum", "braille", "geometric", "technical", "blocks", "sextant",
    "octant", "wedge", "stipple", "border", "dot", "diagonal"
]

SIGNS = ["+", "-"]
SEP = [",", ";"]
WS = ["", " ", "\t", "  "]

# Interesting Unicode ranges: blocks and categories that Chafa often supports
UNICODE_RANGES = [
    (0x0020, 0x007E),   # basic printable ASCII
    (0x00A0, 0x00FF),   # Latin-1 Supplement
    (0x2500, 0x257F),   # Box Drawing
    (0x2580, 0x259F),   # Block Elements
    (0x25A0, 0x25FF),   # Geometric Shapes
    (0x2800, 0x28FF),   # Braille Patterns
    (0x1F300, 0x1F5FF), # Misc Symbols and Pictographs (beyond BMP)
    (0x1F900, 0x1F9FF), # Supplemental Symbols and Pictographs
]

# Convert range to selector tokens like "U+2580-259F" or prefixed with "range:"
def fmt_range(rng: Tuple[int, int], style: int) -> str:
    a, b = rng
    if a > b:
        a, b = b, a
    if style == 0:
        return f"U+{a:X}-U+{b:X}"
    elif style == 1:
        return f"U+{a:X}-{b:X}"
    else:
        return f"range:U+{a:X}-U+{b:X}"

# Render a tag token with optional prefix forms used in various selector syntaxes
# Examples: "tag:block", "+braille", "-ugly", "block"
def fmt_tag(tag: str, mode: int, sign: str | None) -> str:
    if mode == 0:
        return f"tag:{tag}"
    elif mode == 1:
        return f"{sign if sign else ''}{tag}"
    else:
        return tag

# Sometimes combine ranges with tag filters, e.g., "(U+2580-259F)+block" or "braille&wide"
def combine_tokens(left: str, right: str, op: str) -> str:
    return f"{left}{op}{right}"

def rnd_ws(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(WS)

def choose_many(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str], k_min: int, k_max: int) -> List[str]:
    k = rng.randint(k_min, k_max)
    return rng.sample(seq, k=min(k, len(seq)))

def make_clause(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.randint(0, 5)
    if choice == 0:
        # pure tag with optional sign
        tag = rng.choice(TAGS)
        mode = rng.randint(0, 2)
        sign = rng.choice(SIGNS + [None])
        return fmt_tag(tag, mode, sign)
    elif choice == 1:
        # alias group with optional sign
        alias = rng.choice(ALIASES)
        sign = rng.choice(SIGNS + [None])
        return f"{sign if sign else ''}{alias}"
    elif choice in (2, 3):
        # Unicode range
        rng_tuple = rng.choice(UNICODE_RANGES)
        style = rng.randint(0, 2)
        return fmt_range(rng_tuple, style)
    elif choice == 4:
        # Combined: range +/- tag
        left = fmt_range(rng.choice(UNICODE_RANGES), rng.randint(0, 2))
        right = fmt_tag(rng.choice(TAGS), rng.randint(0, 2), rng.choice(SIGNS + [None]))
        op = rng.choice(["+", "-", "&"])  # union, subtract, intersect-like
        return combine_tokens(left, right, op)
    else:
        # Parenthesized sum/diff of a few tags
        parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
            tag = rng.choice(TAGS)
            sign = rng.choice(["+", "-"])
            parts.append(f"{sign}{tag}")
        inner = " ".join(parts)
        return f"({inner})"

def build_expression(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a top-level expression as a list of clauses separated by commas/semicolons
    n_clauses = rng.randint(1, 6)
    clauses = []
    for _ in range(n_clauses):
        clause = make_clause(rng)
        # Occasionally prefix a global sign to the whole clause
        if rng.random() < 0.2 and not clause.startswith("("):
            clause = (rng.choice(SIGNS)) + clause
        # Random whitespace around
        clause = f"{rnd_ws(rng)}{clause}{rnd_ws(rng)}"
        clauses.append(clause)

    # Join with random separators and optional whitespace
    expr = clauses[0]
    for c in clauses[1:]:
        expr += f"{rnd_ws(rng)}{rng.choice(SEP)}{rnd_ws(rng)}{c}"

    # Occasionally append a trailing separator or whitespace to test permissive parsing
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        expr += rng.choice(SEP)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        expr = rnd_ws(rng) + expr + rnd_ws(rng)

    # Ensure overall length <= 4096
    return expr[:4095]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create a mixture of expressions with chances of emphasizing different features
    mode = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if mode == 0:
        # Emphasize tags with signs
        expr_parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
            tag = rng.choice(TAGS)
            sign = rng.choice(SIGNS + [""])
            expr_parts.append(f"{sign}{tag}")
        expr = ",".join(expr_parts)
    elif mode == 1:
        # Emphasize Unicode ranges with different notations
        parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
            parts.append(fmt_range(rng.choice(UNICODE_RANGES), rng.randint(0, 2)))
        expr = "; ".join(parts)
    elif mode == 2:
        # Mix ranges and tags with operators and parentheses
        chunks = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
            left = make_clause(rng)
            right = make_clause(rng)
            op = rng.choice(["+", "-", "&"])
            chunks.append(f"({left}){op}({right})")
        expr = ", ".join(chunks)
    elif mode == 3:
        # Alias-driven selections with exclusions
        picks = choose_many(rng, ALIASES, 2, 6)
        excl = choose_many(rng, TAGS, 1, 3)
        expr = ", ".join(picks + ["-" + e for e in excl])
    else:
        # General expression
        expr = build_expression(rng)

    # Ensure NUL-termination is not needed in Python; the fuzzer wraps as std::string c_str()
    # Return UTF-8 bytes
    data = expr.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: environment vector (char**), entries like KEY=VALUE, NUL-terminated strings,
# final vector terminated by NULL pointer (handled by harness). We only provide a single
# contiguous bytes buffer that fuzzer will sample substrings from via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME.
# Goal: produce a buffer containing multiple plausible KEY=VALUE pairs, with variety,
# lengths, edge cases, and valid UTF-8. Keep under 4096 bytes.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_uppercase + string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_"

COMMON_KEYS = [
    "TERM", "COLORTERM", "LANG", "LC_ALL", "LC_CTYPE", "LC_COLLATE", "LC_NUMERIC",
    "LC_TIME", "LC_MESSAGES", "SHELL", "USER", "HOME", "PATH", "PWD", "OLDPWD",
    "XTERM_VERSION", "TMUX", "TMUX_PANE", "SCREEN", "SSH_CONNECTION", "SSH_TTY",
    "WT_SESSION", "WT_PROFILE_ID", "VTE_VERSION", "TERM_PROGRAM", "TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION",
    "LINUX_KERNEL", "COLUMNS", "LINES", "COLORFGBG", "NO_COLOR",
]

TERM_VALUES = [
    "xterm", "xterm-256color", "screen", "screen-256color", "tmux", "tmux-256color",
    "linux", "vt100", "ansi", "rxvt", "rxvt-unicode", "konsole-256color",
    "xterm-direct", "foot", "wezterm", "alacritty", "kitty", "iterm2",
]

COLORTERM_VALUES = [
    "truecolor", "24bit", "256color", "yes", "", "1",
]

LANG_VALUES = [
    "en_US.UTF-8", "C", "C.UTF-8", "POSIX", "ja_JP.UTF-8", "ru_RU.UTF-8",
    "zh_CN.UTF-8", "de_DE.UTF-8", "fr_FR.UTF-8",
]

# Some escape/control sequences that could appear in environment values but should remain UTF-8 safe
# We'll avoid NUL in entries because C strings must be NUL-terminated by the fuzzer harness.
CONTROL_SAFE = ["\x1b[?25l", "\x1b[0m", "\x1b(B", "\x1b)0"]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "✓", "π", "雪", "🐍", "🖼️", "é", "ç", "ø", "—", "·",
]


def rand_ident(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure starts with letter or underscore for realism
    first = r.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest = "".join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return first + rest


def rand_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a realistic PATH-style value
    parts = []
    n = r.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(n):
        seg_len = r.randint(1, 8)
        seg = "".join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_+") for _ in range(seg_len))
        parts.append("/" + seg)
    return ":".join(parts)


def make_entry(r: random.Random, key: str, value: str) -> str:
    # Ensure no embedded NULs; keep within reasonable length
    kv = f"{key}={value}"
    return kv


def build_env_entries(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    entries: List[str] = []

    # Always include a valid TERM
    term = r.choice(TERM_VALUES)
    entries.append(make_entry(r, "TERM", term))

    # Include LANG/LC_* combinations
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "LANG", r.choice(LANG_VALUES)))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "LC_ALL", r.choice(LANG_VALUES)))
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "LC_CTYPE", r.choice(LANG_VALUES)))

    # Include COLORTERM sometimes
    if r.random() < 0.8:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "COLORTERM", r.choice(COLORTERM_VALUES)))

    # PATH
    if r.random() < 0.9:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "PATH", rand_path(r)))

    # Terminal-specific hints
    if term.startswith("tmux") and r.random() < 0.7:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "TMUX", f"/tmp/tmux-{r.randint(1000,99999)}/{r.randint(0,9)}"))
    if term.startswith("screen") and r.random() < 0.5:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "STY", f"{rand_ident(r)}.{r.randint(0,9999)}"))
    if term in ("kitty", "xterm-direct") and r.random() < 0.6:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "KITTY_WINDOW_ID", str(r.randint(100000, 999999))))

    # Size hints
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "COLUMNS", str(r.randint(40, 300))))
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "LINES", str(r.randint(10, 120))))

    # Include some arbitrary variables with unicode/control-safe sequences
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
        key = rand_ident(r, 3, 10).upper()
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.3:
            val = r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES) * r.randint(1, 3)
        elif choice < 0.6:
            val = r.choice(CONTROL_SAFE)
        else:
            # general ascii token/value
            val = "".join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII + "-.:/") for _ in range(r.randint(1, 24)))
        entries.append(make_entry(r, key, val))

    # Some common fixed keys to trigger code paths
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "TERM_PROGRAM", r.choice(["Apple_Terminal", "iTerm.app", "WezTerm", "foot" ])))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION", f"{r.randint(0,3)}.{r.randint(0,99)}.{r.randint(0,999)}"))

    # Optional empty value and keys with unusual but valid characters
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, rand_ident(r).upper(), ""))
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "COLORFGBG", f"{r.randint(0,15)};{r.randint(0,15)}"))
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        entries.append(make_entry(r, "NO_COLOR", "1"))

    # Add a few random KEY=VALUE pairs for breadth
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)):
        key = r.choice(COMMON_KEYS) if r.random() < 0.5 else rand_ident(r).upper()
        # Build value types
        vt = r.random()
        if vt < 0.25:
            value = str(r.randint(0, 1000000))
        elif vt < 0.5:
            value = rand_path(r)
        elif vt < 0.75:
            value = r.choice(TERM_VALUES)
        else:
            value = "".join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII + "-._:/@") for _ in range(r.randint(1, 40)))
        entries.append(make_entry(r, key, value))

    return entries


def serialize_env(entries: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join with NUL separators and add a final NUL to allow extraction as separate C strings.
    # Many fuzz harnesses pick substrings; having NULs ensures clean termination.
    joined = "\x00".join(entries) + "\x00"
    data = joined.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    # Cap size to 4096 bytes conservatively by truncating at a NUL boundary
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # Find last NUL before limit
        cut = data.rfind(b"\x00", 0, 4096)
        if cut == -1:
            data = data[:4096]
        else:
            data = data[:cut+1]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    entries = build_env_entries(r)
    # Shuffle to vary order and exercise different parsing branches
    r.shuffle(entries)
    return serialize_env(entries)
